evidence: EPRP catalogue (PhanDA slice boundaries on GTS2020, from the PhanSST ReadMe and the main project's PhanDA notes). Observed: slice bounds in the file for Pragian/Lochkovian (410.5-419.0), Emsian base 410.5, Eifelian base 394.3 equal the GTS2020 chart values in docs/primer.md s1.2; the Eifelian/Givetian bound is 385.3.
devonian_and_other_notes: Devonian slice bounds differ from ICS v2024/12 (README table; local/context/timescale_stage_bounds_phanda_phansst.csv); Ordovician and Silurian bounds equal ICS v2024/12 to rounding (primer s1.1). Slices are stage-wide; no conversion applied.

evidence: Observed: PhanSST ReadMe field 'Age: Age, in reference to GTS2020 (Ma)'. Observed: the age range of the points under each Devonian stage label does not follow one scale cleanly (local/context/timescale_stage_bounds_phanda_phansst.csv; for example Pragian points reach 408.6 Ma and Eifelian points 385.7 Ma).
devonian_and_other_notes: derived_stage_label_differs flags points whose Age falls in a different stage on the project's ICS v2024/12 scale from the stage label in the source (294 of 4974 window rows, 162 of them Devonian by age). No age has been changed.

timescale_basis: GTS2012 stage-midpoint ages (inferred); slice label = PALEOMAP plate-model age
evidence: Observed: the 100 maps are labelled by integer Ma (385, 390, ... 450, 460, 470, 480, 490 ...). Inferred: the labels coincide with the 'plate tectonic model age' column of Table 1 in Scotese & Wright (2018), whose stratigraphic ages are 'from Ogg, Ogg & Gradstein (2012)' (GTS2012). The mirror does not name the stage of each temperature map.
devonian_and_other_notes: Treat slice labels as PALEOMAP model ages, not stage-resolved ICS v2024/12 dates. Several Devonian PALEOMAP stage labels (e.g. 410 Ma, 'Pragian, 409.2 Ma') fall in a different stage on ICS v2024/12 (paleodem_slices.csv).

timescale_basis: not stated for the Ordovician-Devonian sheets; Carboniferous-Permian sheets say 'Age (Ma)-2012'
evidence: Observed: sheet headers 'Age (Ma)-2012' on C1-2, C2-P3 and P4-5; plain 'Age (Ma)' on S1-S3 and D1-D3; O5 has 'Age, Ma' (source) and 'Age-updated' (with references). Inferred, not verified against the paper: GTS2012.
devonian_and_other_notes: Devonian ages are interpolated between conodont-zone or stage ages (decimals such as 392.1731); the Emsian-Pragian and Lochkovian-Pragian boundaries move by 2-3 Myr between GTS2012 and ICS v2024/12, so stage labels in D1-D3 do not match the ICS v2024/12 stage of the age for 66 of 325 rows (derived_stage_label_differs). O5 'Age-updated'/'Stage-updated' re-assign late-Katian samples to the Hirnantian at about 442.9 Ma; the filter uses the original 'Age, Ma'.

timescale_basis: GTS2012 for biostratigraphically timed events (article reference 44), but not uniformly
evidence: Observed: article Methods say pre-Quaternary events are 'timed by biostratigraphy with reference to the Geologic Time Scale (44)', reference 44 being Gradstein et al. (2012). Observed: Table 1 gives the K-Pg event at 65.50 Ma, a pre-GTS2012 value (outside the window).
devonian_and_other_notes: Window events (End-Ordovician 445.80, Mulde 428.20, Lau 423.50) are Ordovician-Silurian; no Devonian event in window. Ages are to 0.01 Myr as printed but not that precise.

timescale_basis: GTS2012 for stage boundaries (unless a comment says otherwise); radioisotopic ages as published for LIPs and impacts
evidence: Observed: Table S1 header 'Age reference and comments, if different from GTS2012'; in boundaries.tsv the 'GTS 2012 Age' and 'Age [Ma]' columns are identical for all window rows (empty comment column).
devonian_and_other_notes: derived_ics2024_minus_source_myr gives the shift to the project's scale for each boundary (Pragian/Emsian +3.02, Lochkovian/Pragian +2.22 Myr). LIP and impact ages are absolute radioisotopic ages, not scale-bound, but their stage associations are GTS2012.
